root.name: Sicilian Defense: Chekhover Variation
root.moves: 1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 d6 3. d4 cxd4 4. Qxd4

overview: White recaptures with the queen, avoiding the heavy Open Sicilian theory. After 4...Nc6 5.Bb5 Bd7 6.Bxc6 Bxc6 7.Nc3, White has the more active pieces and Black has a solid position without weaknesses. The play is quiet and positional, with the early queen forced to move again.

white_ideas.idea: Bb5 and Bxc6 to double Black's pawns or fix the structure, then Nc3 and O-O
Use the early queen's central post and a space lead for a small edge

black_ideas.idea: Develop with ...Nc6, ...Nf6 and ...g6 or ...e6 and neutralise the centralised queen
Gain time against the queen and play for ...e5 or ...Nf6-d7 and ...Bg7

typical_structures.structure: White e4 against Black d6/e6 or ...g6, symmetrical-looking Sicilian with a half-open c-file for Black

character.notes: Quiet and simple; known as a way to avoid sharp Sicilian theory. Black has few weaknesses.

structure.notes: Sicilian structure with a half-open c-file; Semi-open.

approach.notes: A real line played occasionally by strong players; standard.

level.notes: Few moves to memorise, plans clear.

sublines_that_differ.name: 4...Nf6
sublines_that_differ.how: Black develops with tempo; the queen faces Nc6 and Qd8 ideas, closer to a Dragon move order.

character.reason: A quiet line with few ways to lose quickly.

structure.reason: An asymmetric Sicilian centre with the half-open c-file.

level.reason: Plans are simple with little theory; could be beginner for White.

plans.reason: White's queen sits centrally and must be kept safe.
